title: Impact analysis
description: What a request touched in the knowledge a repository already held, computed from the objects the analysis wrote. `/5` follows the constructs out of a document and into the base: `record_id` replaces `model_id`, because what names a run is the record holding what has no file, and `implicated[].kind` closes at `domain-object` and `adr`, because a construct is now an object rather than an element of a document held elsewhere. Each entry carries `operation` and `reason`, which is what makes the artifact the map a person reads: a verdict says whether knowledge changed, an operation says what happens to each artifact, and the reason says why that artifact and not another.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

analysis_id.description: Stable identifier for this analysis, supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer: an analysis stamped from a clock could not be repeated and compared.

request_id.description: The request this analysis answers. A request is prose a person supplied plus the material it names; no capability produces one, so the identifier is the caller's to supply.

producer.description: What performed the analysis. Not a const: the contract requires the artifact, not a particular producer of it.

consumer.description: Who reads it. The ingestion reports the verdict and the implicated set before it expands, which is what makes the analysis a step rather than an artifact nobody opens.

verdict.description: Whether permanent knowledge must change at all. A closed field, so a caller branches on a value rather than on a reading of prose. `none` means the knowledge already holds what the request asks for, and is a real outcome rather than a failure.

base_state.description: Whether anything this analysis could implicate existed when it ran. It is an observation, not a judgment: the producer looked and records what was there. It exists because the first request against a repository has nothing to implicate, and a verdict naming nothing is honest there and empty everywhere else. Recorded rather than derived, because the analysis is what observed the state and a later reader cannot re-observe it.

implicated.description: Every artifact this request implicates, by identifier, with what happens to it and why. Identifiers rather than content: restating an artifact here would put a second copy of it in a temporary file, and the copy is the one that stops being maintained.

id.description: The artifact's own identifier, as that artifact declares it. A knowledge object or ADR identifier where the artifact exists; a domain model element identifier where the operation is `create` and no stored artifact answers to it yet.

kind.description: Which contract resolves the identifier. `domain-object` is what the base holds; `adr` is a decision record, which is a graph node and never an object. `knowledge-object` and `domain-model-element` are gone with the profile and the document they named.

operation.description: What this request does to this artifact. The verdict says whether knowledge must change; this says what happens to each thing that changes, which is what a reviewer reads before anything is authored. A change that both narrows an existing artifact and introduces a new one is two entries, because compressing them into one loses the fact that something new appears.

driver.description: The domain model element that causes this entry. Present for `create` and `update`, where a model element is what drives the change. Absent for a `retire` driven by an element the model no longer holds, which is an absence and has no identifier to name.

reason.description: What about this artifact the request makes wrong, incomplete, or absent. `because the request asks for it` is not a reason: it restates that the artifact is in the list. A reason names the property of this artifact that changed, which is the only thing distinguishing a considered entry from a swept-in one.

record_id.description: The analysis this verdict was reached over. It replaces the model identifier the previous version carried: the constructs are files now, and what names the run is the record holding what has no file.

then.description: A verdict that knowledge must change while naming nothing that changes is a verdict with nothing behind it. /2 relaxed this over an empty base because no stored identifier existed to name; /3 removes the relaxation, because `domain-model-element` gives a first analysis identifiers of its own.
`none` states that the knowledge already holds what was asked. An entry alongside it claims something changes, which contradicts the verdict.

Where nothing exists, nothing can be updated and nothing can already hold the answer. The one verdict an empty base admits is `create`, and reporting it as `none` would say the request was answered by knowledge that is not there.
Over a base that held nothing, every entry is a construct this run brought into existence. An entry naming a stored artifact asserts something the observation denies.
